identityReview: Louise Arbour, born 10 February 1947 in Montréal, LL.L. Université de Montréal 1970. Canadian jurist and international prosecutor, not a trial judge at ICTY/ICTR or UN secretary-general. Supreme Court of Canada service 15 September 1999–30 June 2004; human-rights high commissioner 1 July 2004–30 June 2008; Crisis Group 2009–2014; international migration mandate 2017–2018. Current 31st governor general, installed 8 June 2026 following May 5 approval announcement, replacing Mary Simon. The sovereign and prime minister are separate offices.
lifeStatusEvidence: Governor General’s retrospective account records her actual attendance at the National Remembrance Day ceremony in Ottawa on 11 November 2026. This supports recent activity and current office; the earlier attendance notice is not used as proof of a completed event.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read relevant Supreme Court and governor-general biographies, tribunal accession notice and former-prosecutor history, indictment announcement and selected case-information-sheet sections, Canadian migration appointment statement, UN conference conclusion, defence review overview/timeline/release, prime-ministerial approval announcement, installation and actual Remembrance Day records, and justice department prison-inquiry history. Read additional AP installation and Columbia conflict-NGO reporting. Read Commons crop and parent metadata/licensing without image pixels.
corrections: Read the Supreme Court’s birth, qualifications and career entries. LL.L. 1970 is an earned law degree; honorary doctorates are not research PhDs. Its service heading ends 30 June 2004 and its narrative says retired 1 July, compatible last-day/effective-retirement conventions. Use the exact 15 September 1999 appointment rather than the later swearing-in date. Provincial Supreme Court of Ontario is not the national Supreme Court.

Read the current governor-general biography and relevant career sections. Current office begins with the June 8 installation, not the earlier announcement. Its reference to Milošević as Serbian president is imprecise for the May 1999 indictment; the contemporaneous tribunal identifies him as FRY president. Institutional achievements are not solely personal accomplishments. Public education text does not infer an Ottawa graduate degree from graduate studies.

Read the 30 September 1996 tribunal notice. Security Council appointment on February 29 and assumption of prosecutorial duties October 1 are separate. Arbour succeeded Goldstone as prosecutor of both ad hoc tribunals, not their trial judge and not prosecutor of the later International Criminal Court. The press release is a contemporaneous institutional account, not the appointment resolution itself.

Read the Arbour section of the tribunal’s former-prosecutor history. It supports October 1996–September 1999 service and 1 July 2004–30 June 2008 as human-rights high commissioner. Historical award totals are not updated current counts. Neighbouring biographies concern other prosecutors; the impossible September 31 date in the Goldstone section is not copied or used to alter Arbour’s verified October 1 accession.

Read the tribunal’s May 27, 1999 announcement: submission May 22, judicial confirmation May 24, delayed public disclosure May 27. The public profile separates prosecution from conviction and avoids assigning later Bosnia/Croatia charges to this Kosovo indictment. No full indictment evidentiary review or guilt finding is claimed.

Read selected case-information-sheet sections on status, the trial and termination. Milošević died March 11, 2006; proceedings terminated March 14. The 2004 Rule 98bis evidentiary decision was not a final conviction or a blanket acquittal. Do not describe Arbour as the prosecutor conducting the later trial after she left the office.

Read the governor-general career and education chronology. Crisis Group leadership 2009–2014 and migration role 2017–2018 are historical mandates. The public timeline uses year precision for the Crisis Group start; it does not manufacture a day from later appointment announcements. Private-law-firm role is listed 2014–2026, not presumed concurrent current practice after installation. No current ICJ judgeship or unverified research doctorate inferred.

Read Canada’s March 9, 2017 foreign-minister statement confirming appointment as the secretary-general’s special representative for international migration. It is a government congratulatory statement, not the unavailable full UN personnel announcement. Do not confuse international migration with the refugee high commissioner or UN secretary-general.

Read the December 11, 2018 conference-conclusion press release. It confirms the adopted compact, Arbour as conference secretary-general and non-legally-binding status. Conference adoption and later General Assembly endorsement are separate; this document’s forecast of the latter is not proof it had already occurred. Global migration cooperation is not abolition of national borders or compulsory admission quotas.

Read the defence review overview, scope and recommendation sections. Report delivered May 20, 2022; 48 recommendations. Review launch, commissioning, delivery, public release, government acceptance and actual implementation are distinct. The April 29 launch announcement is not silently replaced by the May 20 engagement date in other accounts. No entire report, individual complaints or current implementation audit read.

Read the review timeline’s May 2022 delivery/release and subsequent government-response entries. The initial 17 recommendations moving into implementation did not mean all 48 had been completed. External monitor Jocelyne Therrien is a different person and role; Arbour is not described as the current monitor.

Read the May 30, 2022 release opening and response paragraphs. This is public release, ten days after delivery to the minister. Government language about acceptance and reform intentions is not independent proof of completed cultural change or eradication of misconduct. The 2021 engagement date refers to the prior year, not delivery of the final report.

Read the May 5, 2026 prime-ministerial announcement of the King’s approval on Carney’s recommendation. The future governor-general role is confirmed by a subsequent completed installation record. The governor general represents the sovereign, who is head of state, and is not the elected prime minister. Promotional assessments and current honorary-award totals are not adopted as independently audited facts.

Read the June 8, 2026 retrospective installation record. It confirms the completed Senate ceremony rather than relying on an advance media advisory. Subsequent ceremonial events are not a separate accession date. Original ceremony video was not watched, and the public account does not infer that she was directly elected.

Read the November 11, 2026 activity record confirming attendance at the National War Memorial and commemorative events. This is completed activity, distinct from the November 9 future-tense attendance advisory. Current role and recent life-status evidence are supported by the text; photographic captions are not substituted for viewing image pixels.

Read the justice department’s Kingston inquiry and closure entries. The inquiry concerned 1994 events, with appointment in 1995; the 1996 report year is cross-checked with the current official biography. The 2000 prison closure followed a reform process dating to the 1990 task force. Do not credit Arbour alone with initiating every reform or attribute all national penal policy changes to one report.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original birth certificate or diploma, full inquiry or military-review report, complete trial evidence, current implementation audit, appointment instrument, full installation video or portrait pixels reviewed. Do not transform prosecutorial allegations into judgments, institutional recognition into sole personal credit, non-binding compact into a treaty obligation, or reform proposals into completed outcomes.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields reviewed in seven foreign languages against Chinese and English. Preserve LL.L. versus honorary doctorates; provincial and national courts; 1996 appointment versus accession and prosecutor versus judge; May 1999 submission/confirmation/disclosure and 2006 death/termination without final judgment; 1995 inquiry/1996 report versus earlier reform and 2000 closure; last Supreme Court service day versus next-day retirement; human-rights versus refugee commissioner; conference versus UN secretary-general and non-binding compact; 2022 delivery/public release/recommendations versus implementation; May 2026 approval versus June installation; governor general versus monarch and prime minister; November actual ceremony versus advance notice.
